LATTICE SEMICONDUCTOR REPORTS RECORD 3Q26 REVENUE, UP 118% YOY

Record FPGA Revenue, Up Approximately 90% YOY, Led by Compute and Communications Demand

Expects Approximately 130% YOY Revenue Growth in 4Q26, with Industrial and Embedded Revenue Growth Accelerating to 70% YOY 

 

HILLSBORO, Ore. – Nov. 2, 2026 – Lattice Semiconductor Corporation (Nasdaq: LSCC), the low power programmable and platform firmware leader, announced financial results today for the fiscal third quarter ended October 3, 2026.

 

Lattice completed the acquisition of AMI on July 27, 2026 (the “acquisition date”). Lattice’s results for the third quarter of fiscal 2026 include AMI’s results from the acquisition date, while the prior periods presented do not.

 

Revenue for the third quarter of 2026 was $291.0 million, with GAAP gross margin of 67.4%, and GAAP net income per diluted share of $0.08. On a non-GAAP basis, gross margin was 70.9%, with net income per diluted share of $0.72. GAAP net income and GAAP net income margin for the third quarter of 2026 were $11.2 million and 3.9%, respectively, with adjusted EBITDA of $131.0 million, which is a 45.0% adjusted EBITDA margin for the third quarter of 2026. GAAP net cash flow from operating activities and operating cash flow margin for the third quarter of 2026 were $95.0 million and 32.7%, respectively, which corresponds to non-GAAP free cash flow and free cash flow margin of $77.6 million and 26.7%, respectively.

 

Ford Tamer, Chief Executive Officer, said, "We delivered record third quarter revenue of $291 million and non-GAAP EPS of $0.72, up 118% and approximately 160% year-over-year, respectively. FPGA revenue grew approximately 90%, fueled by accelerating data center AI demand and continued momentum across Industrial & Embedded applications. Strong bookings, backlog and design wins support our fourth-quarter revenue outlook of approximately $335 million and reinforce our confidence in growth into 2027 and beyond. The addition of AMI meaningfully expands our opportunity in security, control and management solutions. Early commercial momentum across security retrofit, rack boot, plug and play, and power and cooling demonstrates the value of our combined portfolio, positioning Lattice to capture greater content per platform, deepen strategic customer relationships and drive sustainable long-term growth."

 

Lorenzo Flores, Chief Financial Officer, said, "Lattice’s operating leverage was evident in the third quarter as we translated accelerating demand into faster year-over-year earnings growth. We continue to execute against our growth strategy by investing to strengthen our leadership in small and mid-range FPGAs, expanding our combined Lattice and AMI solutions portfolio, and advancing our companion chip opportunity. Our focus remains on driving profitable growth, expanding free cash flow, reducing debt, and delivering long-term shareholder value."

Third Quarter 2026 Highlights:

  •

Achieved Record New Product Revenue Growth: Revenue from new products grew more than 70% year over year and is tracking to reach 25% of FPGA revenue in 2026, led by AI-related server demand and Industrial and Embedded accelerated recovery. 
  • Hosted Two Technical Summits in Taipei and Shenzhen with Lattice and AMI: Over 700 customers and partners attended the two events, with presentations from Advantech, Inovance, Intel, Mitsubishi Electric, NVIDIA, NXP Semiconductors, Panasonic, Qualcomm and Sony. Demonstrated over 20 solutions, showing the power of Lattice companion chip and AMI companion firmware ecosystem.
  • Advanced Secure Control and Management at OCP Global Summit with Other Industry Leaders: Announced the Secure Control and Management Plane (SCMP), with AMD, Arm, ASPEED, Intel, Jabil, Microsoft, and NXP Semiconductor. Brought Lattice and AMI together with keynote, technical presentation and demonstrations.
  • Expanded AI Infrastructure Collaboration with Arm: Announced a collaboration combining Arm AGI CPU server platforms, Lattice FPGAs and AMI firmware to deliver secure control, management and connectivity for next-generation AI data centers.
  • Accelerated FPGA Development with AI: Launched Lattice Prompt, enabling natural-language access across the FPGA design flow and productivity gains of 10X or more on common design tasks.

 

2
 

 

 Third Quarter 2026 Highlights (continued):

  • Extended Secure Control FPGA Leadership: Introduced the Lattice Mach-N2 family, combining integrated flash, hardware Root of Trust and post-quantum cryptography with greater logic density and connectivity. Samples have shipped to leading Compute & Communications customers.
  • Expanded Quantum-Resistant Platform Security: Released Lattice Sentry 5.0, the industry’s first PQC-enabled platform firmware resilience and attestation solution, combining Lattice FPGAs with AMI software to protect AI infrastructure and simplify secure deployment.
  • Recognized for Post-Quantum Cryptography Security: Lattice MachXO5-NX TDQ FPGAs won the 2026 CyberSecurity Breakthrough Award for Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) Solution of the Year.
  • Broadened AI Infrastructure Support with AMD: Announced fully validated AMI Rack Manager support for AMD Helios rackscale solutions and Aptio V and MegaRAC OneTree firmware support for 6th Gen AMD EPYC processors, simplifying deployment and enabling secure boot, monitoring and management for next-generation AI data centers.
  • Launched Rack-Scale AI Infrastructure Management: Introduced AMI Rack Manager 1.0 at AMI Tech Summit 2026 in Taipei, providing centralized monitoring, management and automation across diverse rack infrastructure. Expanded visibility into rack health, power and thermal conditions to simplify deployment and optimize resource utilization.
  • Strengthened Data Center Memory Resilience with SK Hynix: Announced production-ready support for the SK Hynix RAS Library in AMI MegaRAC OneTree, integrating proactive memory error management, runtime repair and page-offlining to improve server reliability, simplify maintenance and reduce total cost of ownership.
  • Expanded Data Center Management Capabilities: Released AMI Data Center Manager 6.2, combining fleet-wide BIOS configuration, enhanced firmware provisioning and advanced GPU diagnostics with expanded power and thermal monitoring to simplify large-scale infrastructure operations and improve efficiency across AI and enterprise data centers.

 

Business Outlook - Fourth Quarter of 2026:

  •

Lattice revenue for the fourth quarter of 2026 is expected to be between $325 million and $345 million.
  • Lattice gross margin for the fourth quarter of 2026 is expected to be 72.0% plus or minus 1% on a non-GAAP basis.
  • Total operating expenses for the fourth quarter of 2026 are expected to be between $95 million and $101 million on a non-GAAP basis.
  • Income tax rate for the fourth quarter of 2026 is expected to be between 4% and 6% on a non-GAAP basis.
  • Net income for the fourth quarter of 2026 is expected to be between $0.82 and $0.86 per share on a non-GAAP basis.

Non-GAAP Financial Measures: In addition to financial measures prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP), this earnings release makes reference to non-GAAP financial measures. With respect to the outlook for the fourth quarter of 2026, certain items that affect reconciliation of non-GAAP financial measures for non-GAAP gross margin percentage, non-GAAP total operating expenses, non-GAAP income tax rate, non-GAAP EPS, and non-GAAP net income are not available on a forward-looking basis because such items cannot be reasonably calculated without unreasonable efforts due to the unpredictability of the amounts and timing of events affecting the items we exclude from non-GAAP financial measures, including certain large and/or unpredictable charges such as stock-based compensation expense; performance-based equity expense; legal expense outside the ordinary course of business; amortization of acquired intangible assets; restructuring; impairment and acquisition related charges; write-off of unamortized debt costs; and the estimated tax effect of these items, non-cash changes in net deferred income taxes, and other tax adjustments. Consequently, the Company is unable to calculate the most directly comparable GAAP measure to non-GAAP gross margin percentage, non-GAAP total operating expenses, non-GAAP income tax rate, non-GAAP EPS, and non-GAAP net income for the Company’s fourth quarter of 2026 guidance.

Non-GAAP Financial Measures:

Included within this press release and the accompanying tables and notes are certain non-GAAP financial measures that supplement the Company's consolidated financial information prepared in accordance with U.S. GAAP, including non-GAAP gross margin, gross margin percentage, R&D expense percentage, SG&A expense percentage, operating expenses, income from operations, income from operations percentage, interest (expense) income, net, other (expense) income, net, income tax expense, net income, net income per share – basic, and net income per share – diluted, adjusted EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA margin, free cash flow, and free cash flow margin. The non-GAAP measures presented exclude charges and adjustments primarily related to stock-based compensation and related payroll tax effects; accruals related to the portion of our annual incentive plan that we intend to settle in shares of our common stock; transformation activities; legal expense outside the ordinary course of business; amortization of acquired intangible assets; restructuring plan and other charges; acquisition related charges, write-off of unamortized debt costs; bridge facility debt cost amortization, and the estimated tax effect of these items, non-cash changes in net deferred income taxes, change in tax law and other tax adjustments; and depreciation and other amortization. These charges and adjustments are a result of periodic or non-core operating activities of the Company. The Company describes these non-GAAP financial measures and reconciles them to the most directly comparable GAAP measures in the tables and notes attached to this press release.

The Company's management believes that these non-GAAP financial measures provide an additional and useful way of viewing aspects of our performance that, when viewed in conjunction with our GAAP results, provide a more comprehensive understanding of the various factors and trends affecting our ongoing financial performance and operating results than GAAP measures alone. Management also uses these non-GAAP measures for strategic and business decision-making, internal budgeting, forecasting, and resource allocation processes and believes that investors should have access to similar data. The non-GAAP financial information used by the Company may differ from that used by other companies. These non-GAAP measures are included solely for informational and comparative purposes and are not meant as a substitute for GAAP and should be considered together with the consolidated financial information located in the tables attached to this press release.

About Lattice Semiconductor Corporation:

Lattice Semiconductor (Nasdaq: LSCC) is the low power programmable and platform firmware leader. We solve customer challenges from the Edge to the Cloud, in the growing Compute, Communications, Industrial, and Embedded markets. With the addition of AMI's industry-leading, silicon-neutral platform firmware and infrastructure manageability solutions, Lattice now delivers the industry's most complete secure management and control platform for cloud and AI data center infrastructure. Our technology, long-standing relationships, and commitment to world-class support let our customers quickly and easily unleash their innovation to create a smart, secure, and connected world. For more information about Lattice, please visit www.latticesemi.com and follow us via LinkedIn, X, YouTube, Facebook, WeChat, and Weibo.

Lattice Semiconductor previously announced that it has updated its disaggregated end market reporting to better reflect how the Company views its business. Effective Q1 2026, Lattice Semiconductor began disaggregating revenue by end market into (i) Compute and Communications and (ii) Industrial and Embedded. Compute and Communications reflects a reordering of the Company's prior Communications and Computing end market, while Industrial and Embedded combines the Company's previously reported Industrial and Automotive, and Consumer end markets. This change represented a presentation-only update and had no impact on the Company’s consolidated financial results. Prior period end market information has been recast to conform to the new presentation to facilitate comparability.

 

Lattice completed its acquisition of AMI on July 27, 2026. AMI revenue reflects revenue recognized following the acquisition date and is presented as a separate end market beginning in the third quarter of 2026 to enhance comparability with prior disclosures.
